description: Complex WHERE/GROUP BY/ORDER BY/LIMIT combinations and DISTINCT aggregates (COUNT/SUM/AVG DISTINCT, with GROUP BY, NULLs, multiples). Converted 1:1 from query/ComplexQueryTest and DistinctAggregateTest (both now retired; loose >=/<= row asserts pinned to the deterministic exact counts).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, salary INTEGER, age INTEGER)

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'Engineering', 90000, 30), (2, 'Bob', 'Sales', 70000, 35), (3, 'Charlie', 'Engineering', 95000, 28), (4, 'Diana', 'Sales', 75000, 32), (5, 'Eve', 'Engineering', 85000, 29), (6, 'Frank', 'HR', 65000, 40)
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 70000 ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 2
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, salary INTEGER, age INTEGER)

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'Engineering', 90000, 30), (2, 'Bob', 'Sales', 70000, 35), (3, 'Charlie', 'Engineering', 95000, 28), (4, 'Diana', 'Sales', 75000, 32), (5, 'Eve', 'Engineering', 85000, 29), (6, 'Frank', 'HR', 65000, 40)
SELECT department, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY department ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 2
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, salary INTEGER, age INTEGER)

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'Engineering', 90000, 30), (2, 'Bob', 'Sales', 70000, 35), (3, 'Charlie', 'Engineering', 95000, 28), (4, 'Diana', 'Sales', 75000, 32), (5, 'Eve', 'Engineering', 85000, 29), (6, 'Frank', 'HR', 65000, 40)
SELECT department, AVG(salary), COUNT(*) FROM employees WHERE age < 35 GROUP BY department ORDER BY AVG(salary) DESC LIMIT 2
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, salary INTEGER, age INTEGER)

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'Engineering', 90000, 30), (2, 'Bob', 'Sales', 70000, 35), (3, 'Charlie', 'Engineering', 95000, 28), (4, 'Diana', 'Sales', 75000, 32), (5, 'Eve', 'Engineering', 85000, 29), (6, 'Frank', 'HR', 65000, 40)
SELECT department, COUNT(*), AVG(salary), MAX(salary), MIN(age) FROM employees WHERE salary >= 70000 GROUP BY department
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, salary INTEGER, age INTEGER)

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'Engineering', 90000, 30), (2, 'Bob', 'Sales', 70000, 35), (3, 'Charlie', 'Engineering', 95000, 28), (4, 'Diana', 'Sales', 75000, 32), (5, 'Eve', 'Engineering', 85000, 29), (6, 'Frank', 'HR', 65000, 40)
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE (department = 'Engineering' AND salary > 85000) OR (department = 'Sales' AND age > 30)
